description: idf-analysis is a Python package for estimating rainfall intensity-duration-frequency curves. The JOSS article connects these curves to urban drainage and hydraulic-structure design, and the own repository provides package and documentation links. Spatial coverage is the rain-gauge or gridded rainfall source selected; temporal coverage is its observation period and extrapolated return periods. The own repository reports MIT. A planner can use the output as design rainfall input for storm-sewer or flood-defence simulations. A caveat is that rare-event estimates have uncertainty from record length and fitted distribution, especially if climate conditions change. A curve does not represent how runoff moves through a catchment or a sewer network. The software requires rainfall observations from a separate source. No directly related catalogue record was established. The article and own repository were read without downloading gauges or fitting an IDF curve.
name: idf-analysis heavy-rainfall curves
